name: Production Distro RC10
source: RC9 final audit; TASK.md; maestro-managed continuation
goal: Publish a real immutable external HTTPS object descriptor for AIOS payload bytes, reconcile drift to zero, verify installer quarantine fetch, enroll at least two canary targets, bind exact approval to AgentCore and SecurityExecutionEngine, and produce controlled canary activation plus rollback evidence.
core_thesis: AIOS becomes distributable only when public metadata points to immutable bytes, the installer verifies those bytes locally before interpretation, and every activation or rollback side effect is constrained by exact approval, AgentCore PlanSpec, SecurityExecutionEngine policy, rollback, audit, and support/recovery bindings.
non_goals: Do not claim GA production readiness.
Do not read, copy, print, hash, move, or reference private signing material.
Do not turn the mirror host into large object storage or a signing authority.
Do not combine mirror and signer authority.
Do not embed credential-bearing, mutable, local, or short-lived signed URLs in persistent metadata.
Do not let frontend, mirror, signer reachability, shell output, model replay, or TUI output become authority.
Do not mutate production rings during RC10 planning or contract work.
primary_acceptance: RC10 defines the enablement boundary for real immutable external object publication while preserving metadata-only mirror semantics.
RC10 requires declared/current artifact drift to be zero before external object trust, installer authorization, activation, or rollback.
RC10 requires installer quarantine fetch verification before payload interpretation.
RC10 requires at least two enrolled canary targets before controlled activation.
RC10 requires exact operator approval, AgentCore PlanSpec, and SecurityExecutionEngine effect envelope before side effects.
RC10 requires separate rollback approval and support/recovery binding before rollback execution.
RC10 keeps production_ready_claim=false unless final audit proves every GA gate.
